question: What is the name of India’s first indigenous aircraft carrier?
solution:
The correct answer is __**INS Vikrant**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The name of India's first indigenous aircraft carrier is INS Vikrant.
 
• The ship was launched on August 12, 2013, acquired on July 28, 2022, and commissioned on September 2, 2022. 
 
• The name Vikrant comes from the Sanskrit word vikrānta which means "courageous" or "bold".
 
• The name was also used for India's first aircraft carrier, which was commissioned in 1961. 
 
• The ship is 262 meters long and has a carrying capacity of 40,000 metric tons. 
 
• The ship can accommodate up to 30 aircraft, including the MiG-29K fighter jets, Kamov-31 helicopters, and MH-60R multi-role helicopters. 
 
• The ship was built at Cochin Shipyard Limited and has an indigenous content of 76%. 
 
• The ship has a ski-jump for launching aircraft and a set of "arrester wires" for recovering them.
 
• It also uses a novel aircraft-operation mode called STOBAR (Short Take-Off but Arrested Landing)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• INS Viraat
 
 
• Type: Aircraft Carrier
 
• Commissioned: May 12, 1987 (into the Indian Navy)
 
• Decommissioned: March 6, 2017
 
• Notable Features:
 
• Originally commissioned in the Royal Navy as HMS Hermes in 1959.
 
• Played a significant role in various operations, including Operation Jupiter in Sri Lanka (1989) and Operation Parakram (2001–2002).
 
• It was the flagship of the Indian Navy for nearly 30 years.
 
 
 
• INS Visakhapatnam
 
 
• Type: Guided Missile Destroyer (Project 15B Class)
 
• Commissioned: November 21, 2021
 
• Notable Features:
 
• Equipped with state-of-the-art weapons and sensors, including BrahMos missiles and Barak-8 air defense systems.
 
• Incorporates stealth technologies to reduce radar and infrared signatures.
 
• Designed for multi-role operations including anti-air, anti-surface, and anti-submarine warfare.
 
 
 
• INS Vijaya
 
 
• Type: Patrol Vessel
 
• Commissioned: September 2018
 
• Notable Features:
 
• Second ship of the Saryu-class offshore patrol vessels (OPVs).
 
• Designed for coastal and offshore surveillance, anti-piracy operations, and maritime patrolling.
 
• Equipped with modern navigation and communication systems.
